title: NPM
body:
*Node Package Manager* — the registry of JavaScript [[Package]]s and the command-line tool
that installs them. It ships with [[Node.js]], and the "very rich ecosystem" argument for Node
is really an argument about npm.

```bash
npm init          # creates package.json
npm install express     # adds it to dependencies and to node_modules
npm install           # installs everything package.json lists
```

Two files come out of it. `package.json` is the manifest you edit: name, version, entry point,
scripts, and the dependency ranges you are willing to accept. `package-lock.json` is generated
and pins the **exact** version of every package and every package's packages, so a second
machine running `npm install` builds the same tree rather than a newer one.

Installing one package pulls in its whole dependency graph, which is why `node_modules` is
enormous and why a tiny project can end up with several hundred packages in it. The registry
is public and mostly unvetted; anyone can publish, which is the security cost that comes with
the convenience.

Built-in modules (`http`, `fs`, `path`, `url`) need no install. Everything else, [[Express]]
included, does. See [[Module]] for what `require` actually hands back.
